critical_code_review_comments: canva_module.py:36-41 — _external_host() trusts the X-Forwarded-Host header without validating it. In an ingress/CDN setup this is normally fine, but if an attacker can inject the header on the /connect call the resulting redirect_uri on Canva's side will differ from the one recomputed on /callback (both derived the same way) so tokens still work — however the redirect_uri registered with Canva must match. Consider pinning to an env var (e.g. PUBLIC_HOST) for defense-in-depth.

canva_module.py:117-121 — code_verifier is built with urlsafe_b64encode on 48 random bytes producing a 64-char string, which is fine. Consider using secrets.token_urlsafe(64) for readability; behaviour unchanged.

canva_module.py:149-151 — oauth state documents in db.canva_oauth_states are never TTL-indexed. They will accumulate indefinitely (only successful callbacks delete them; error/timeout paths leak). Add a TTL index on created_at (expireAfterSeconds ~ 900) or delete on failure branches.

canva_module.py:180-191 — refresh_token is persisted in cleartext in MongoDB. This mirrors Stripe key handling elsewhere in the project but is worth flagging: consider encrypting at rest or scoping the field with a projection guard so it never leaks via a stray find_one({}).

canva_module.py:200-203 — GET /designs returns the raw Canva payload including any continuation cursor. The frontend only reads data.items — fine, but consider whitelisting fields to avoid leaking Canva-side metadata (owner ids, urls) to the client if Canva changes their shape.
